title: Le printemps arrive - premiers signes
oneGoal: Students will observe and identify the first signs that spring is beginning in our environment
decisionPoints: What early spring signs are visible around our school today?
Should we start with temperature observations or outdoor exploration?
Are students ready to compare winter and spring conditions?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces spring observation skills and core vocabulary through direct environmental contact
realWorldConnection: How families notice spring arriving through warmer weather and longer days

title: Les bourgeons réveillent
oneGoal: Students will observe buds on trees and understand that plants are waking up from winter rest
decisionPoints: Which trees show the clearest bud development in our area?
Should we examine buds up close or observe from a distance first?
Are students ready for before-and-after bud comparison activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing specifically on tree changes while introducing plant awakening concepts
realWorldConnection: Observing how trees in our neighborhood begin to change as winter ends

title: Pourquoi les plantes se réveillent-elles?
oneGoal: Students will understand that plants wake up in spring because they get more sun and warmth
decisionPoints: How can we make sun and warmth needs concrete for young learners?
Should we use plant growth experiments or simple demonstrations?
Are students ready for basic cause-and-effect discussions about plant needs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by introducing simple scientific explanations for plant awakening through hands-on experiences
realWorldConnection: Understanding why gardens start growing when the weather gets warmer

title: Les premières feuilles vertes
oneGoal: Students will observe the emergence of new green leaves and understand this shows healthy plant growth
decisionPoints: Which plants show the most obvious new leaf growth?
Should we focus on one type of plant or compare multiple species?
Are students ready for leaf shape and size observation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by applying plant growth understanding to observe actual leaf development
realWorldConnection: Watching trees and bushes around our homes get green leaves in springtime

title: Il fait plus chaud - mesurer le printemps
oneGoal: Students will observe that spring brings warmer temperatures and learn to measure temperature changes
decisionPoints: What temperature measuring tools work best for Grade 1 students?
Should we compare morning and afternoon temperatures?
Are students ready for simple temperature recording activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by expanding observations to include temperature while introducing measurement tools
realWorldConnection: How warmer spring temperatures affect our clothing choices and outdoor activities

title: Les jours deviennent plus longs
oneGoal: Students will observe that daylight hours increase in spring and understand how this affects living things
decisionPoints: How can we make daylight changes visible to young students?
Should we track sunrise/sunset times or use classroom observations?
Are students ready for before-and-after daylight comparisons?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by exploring how increased sunlight affects the environment and living things
realWorldConnection: Noticing how we can play outside longer and don't need lights on as early

title: Les animaux se réveillent aussi
oneGoal: Students will observe how animals become more active in spring as they emerge from winter rest
decisionPoints: Which local animals show obvious spring activity increases?
Should we observe real animals or use photos and videos?
Are students ready for animal behavior prediction activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by connecting environmental changes to animal responses while introducing spring activity concepts
realWorldConnection: Seeing more birds, insects, and small animals active outside our homes

title: Les oiseaux construisent des nids
oneGoal: Students will understand that spring is nesting season and observe bird nest-building behaviors
decisionPoints: Which nesting birds can students safely observe in our area?
Should we focus on nest materials or nest locations?
Are students ready for simple bird behavior observation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by exploring specific animal spring behavior (nesting) while reinforcing observation skills
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we see birds gathering sticks and building nests in trees

title: Pourquoi faire des nids au printemps?
oneGoal: Students will understand that animals make nests in spring to prepare for their babies
decisionPoints: How can we explain animal reproduction appropriately for Grade 1?
Should we use nest examples or focus on animal family concepts?
Are students ready for discussions about animal care and protection?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring why animals nest in spring while introducing family and care concepts
realWorldConnection: Learning how animal families take care of their babies like human families do

title: Expérience: faire pousser des graines
oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to grow seeds and understand how plants begin life in spring
decisionPoints: Which seeds are most appropriate for quick classroom germination?
Should we plant seeds individually or in groups?
Are students ready for daily observation and recording activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by conducting plant growth experiments while understanding how new life begins in spring
realWorldConnection: Learning how gardens and farms start growing food in springtime

title: Les fleurs apparaissent
oneGoal: Students will observe spring flowers and understand they help plants make new seeds
decisionPoints: Which spring flowers are safest and most accessible for observation?
Should we focus on flower colors, shapes, or scents first?
Are students ready for discussions about why flowers are colorful?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by connecting plant growth to flower production while reinforcing observation skills
realWorldConnection: Enjoying the beautiful flowers that bloom in our gardens and parks each spring

title: Les insectes reviennent
oneGoal: Students will observe that insects become active in spring and understand their connection to flowers
decisionPoints: Which insects are safest for students to observe in our area?
Should we focus on beneficial insects or observe all spring insects?
Are students ready for discussions about insect-flower relationships?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by connecting flowers to insects while exploring another aspect of spring awakening
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we see more bees, butterflies, and other insects when flowers bloom

title: Notre jardin de printemps
oneGoal: Students will plan and start a spring garden to observe plant growth throughout the season
decisionPoints: What plants are most appropriate for our classroom spring garden?
Should we plant vegetables, flowers, or herbs?
Are students ready for ongoing plant care responsibilities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by applying all spring learning to create and tend an actual garden
realWorldConnection: Learning how families grow food and flowers in their own gardens

title: Notre livre scientifique de printemps
oneGoal: Students will create a class science book documenting all their spring observations and discoveries
decisionPoints: What format works best for student spring science documentation?
Should we include drawings, photos, or written observations?
Are students ready for collaborative book creation activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all learning into scientific documentation while practicing science communication
realWorldConnection: How scientists share their discoveries by writing and drawing what they learn about nature

title: Prédictions: que va-t-il se passer en été?
oneGoal: Students will use their spring observations to make scientific predictions about summer changes (extension)
decisionPoints: Which predictions can students reasonably make based on spring observations?
Should we focus on plant, animal, or weather predictions?
Are students ready for hypothesis-making based on evidence?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies learning to make scientific predictions while reinforcing observation skills
realWorldConnection: How understanding spring changes helps us prepare for and predict summer conditions

title: Printemps autour du monde
oneGoal: Students will explore how spring looks different in various climates and regions (extension)
decisionPoints: Which global spring examples are most accessible to Grade 1 students?
Should we use photos, videos, or maps to explore different regions?
Are students ready for climate comparison activities?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - broadens perspective on seasonal changes while applying observation vocabulary to global contexts
realWorldConnection: Understanding that spring happens around the world but looks different in different places

title: Expérience: créer des conditions de printemps
oneGoal: Students will design experiments to recreate spring conditions and observe their effects (extension)
decisionPoints: What spring conditions can students safely recreate in classroom experiments?
Should we focus on warmth, light, or water changes?
Are students ready for experiment design rather than just following procedures?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - advances to experiment design while reinforcing understanding of spring environmental factors
realWorldConnection: Learning how scientists use controlled conditions to understand how plants and animals respond to spring

title: Le printemps et les humains
oneGoal: Students will investigate how humans adapt their behaviors and activities for spring changes (extension)
decisionPoints: Which human spring adaptations are most visible to students?
Should we focus on clothing, activities, or food changes?
Are students ready for comparing human and animal spring behaviors?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - connects seasonal changes to human behavior while comparing with animal adaptations studied earlier
realWorldConnection: Understanding how our families change their routines, clothing, and activities for spring weather

title: Présentation scientifique de printemps
oneGoal: Students will present their spring science discoveries to others using scientific language and evidence (extension)
decisionPoints: What format best allows students to share their spring learning?
Should presentations focus on individual discoveries or group findings?
Are students ready for answering questions about their observations?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - culminates learning through scientific communication while practicing presentation skills
realWorldConnection: How scientists share their research with other people to help everyone understand nature better

title: Fête des petits scientifiques de printemps
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their spring science journey with families by sharing experiments and discoveries (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration showcase each student's scientific growth?
Should we include live plant demonstrations or displays of completed work?
What activities best demonstrate student learning to families?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates the complete science unit while building community connections and scientific confidence
realWorldConnection: How sharing our science learning with families helps build community understanding of nature and seasonal changes
